passes.notes: Answer A teaches the three untouched units first. During those weeks, calculations comes back every Friday, and drug classes and law alternate on Saturdays. From Week 5 it mixes all six units together, and every review is active recall plus an error log, with no invented exam details. Answer B covers the new units and then reviews each old unit in its own block. Law disappears until Week 7, and topics barely recur, though B's single week-by-week table is easier to read on a fridge.

B keeps all three previously studied units in the plan from week 1: calculations every Friday, with drug classes and law alternating on Saturdays. It then moves to interleaved mixed practice and builds active recall into every session. A drops drug classes and law entirely for weeks 1–4 and then reviews each in its own block, which weakens spaced review, though its day-level topic detail is useful. B also leaves exam length and passing score as placeholders instead of assuming them, while A only partly flags such details by pointing the learner to the official blueprint.
